newsitem.title: USA: US stocks seen opening up as bull market forges on.
newsitem.headline: US stocks seen opening up as bull market forges on.

text.p: After taking a mild breather on Thursday, Wall Street stocks are expected to open higher on Friday with no major factors seen knocking the market's recent furious bull trend.
Standard & Poor's 500 December futures were up 0.9 to 746.35. The benchmark 30-year bond was slightly lower, off two ticks to yield 6.42 percent.
The Dow industrials stepped back a bit from recent record heights and closed off 12 to about 6418 on Thursday.
"We're probably headed for a higher opening. But I'm hoping for some profit-taking later in the session," said Peter Cardillo, director of research at Westfalia Investments.
"We've got import/export numbers coming in later, but I don't expect that to have much effect," he said.

At 1000 EST/1500 GMT, the government reports import and export prices for October. At 1400 EST/1900 GMT, federal budget data is due. Economists expects a deficit of about $32.00 billion, compared to a surplus of $35.37 billion in the previous report.

Record short interest on the New York Stock Exchange in November points to more investors betting U.S. stocks will have to pull back from their recent record levels. The has Dow hit 10 record closing highs so far in November.

The NYSE said November short interest of 2.8 billion shares, shattering October's previous all-time high of 2,563,918,771 shares. Investors covering their short bets could also be contributing to November's record stock levels, Cardillo said.
He also cited a recent report that the number of Wall Street bulls increased substantially, which made him fear a looming correction was nearing.
"But I don't see anything out there today to provoke a reversal," he said.
In Tokyo, the Nikkei Average of 225 leading stocks rose almost 73 points to 21,216, its highest level of the day.
In London, the FTSE 100 Index surged, up 40 to 3994.
U.S. shares traded in London were somewhat sluggish, but momentum continued in IBM Corp's phenomenal ascent, with the stock rising 1/8. Intel rose /14 to 119-1/8.
The dollar held on to small gains against the yen in Asia trading and struggling to remain above 1.50 marks in Europe.

The Wall Street Journal's Heard on the Street column says some are urging Marsh & McLennan Cos Inc, which has been beset by sagging insurance profits, to free its successful Putnam Investments mutual fund operations.

The New York Times writes that the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission is sending a message to companies that if they should report if they pay bribes or do now allow them to distort financial statements.
